tool.name: falcoAmadeus
tool.description: Sequencing-aware, FastQC-compatible quality control with correct paired-end analysis
tool.command: #import re #if str($mode.mode_select) == 'single' #set input_name_sl = re.sub('[^\w\-\s]', '_', str($mode.input_file.element_identifier)) #if 'bam' in $mode.input_file.ext #set format = 'bam' #elif 'sam' in $mode.input_file.ext #set format = 'sam' #elif str($mode.input_file.ext).endswith('.gz') #set format = 'fastq.gz' #else #set format = 'fastq' #end if ln -s '${mode.input_file}' '${input_name_sl}' && #else #set sample_name = re.sub('[^\w\-]', '_', str($mode.input_pair.name or 'sample')) or 'sample' #set fwd_gz = str($mode.input_pair.forward.ext).endswith('.gz') #set rev_gz = str($mode.input_pair.reverse.ext).endswith('.gz') #if $fwd_gz #set r1 = 'r1.fastq.gz' #else #set r1 = 'r1.fastq' #end if ln -s '${mode.input_pair.forward}' '${r1}' && ## falcoAmadeus 3 aborts on an uncompressed R1 combined with a gzipped R2, ## so that one mate combination is normalised by decompressing R2. #if $rev_gz and not $fwd_gz #set r2 = 'r2.fastq' gzip -cd '${mode.input_pair.reverse}' > '${r2}' && #elif $rev_gz #set r2 = 'r2.fastq.gz' ln -s '${mode.input_pair.reverse}' '${r2}' && #else #set r2 = 'r2.fastq' ln -s '${mode.input_pair.reverse}' '${r2}' && #end if #end if mkdir out && falcoAmadeus --outdir out --threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} --quiet #if $contaminants --contaminants '${contaminants}' #end if #if $adapters --adapters '${adapters}' #end if #if $limits --limits '${limits}' #end if $nogroup #if str($assay) != 'generic' --assay '${assay}' #if str($assay) in ('wgbs', 'emseq', 'rrbs') -conversion-residual $conversion_residual #end if #end if #if $subsample > 1 -subsample $subsample #end if $bisulfite $reverse_complement #if str($mode.mode_select) == 'single' $mode.generate_summary -f '${format}' '${input_name_sl}' #else --name '${sample_name}' --paired-data '${mode.paired_data}' --paired-with '${r2}' '${r1}' #if str($mode.paired_data) != 'combined' && mv out/'${sample_name}'_forward/fastqc_data.txt out/forward_fastqc_data.txt && mv out/'${sample_name}'_reverse/fastqc_data.txt out/reverse_fastqc_data.txt #end if #end if

param.name: mode_select
param.label: Input type
param.help: Paired mode analyses a forward/reverse pair together: in addition to the usual per-mate analysis it runs a lockstep pass over both mates and reports a corrected paired-end PCR-duplication rate (a pair only counts as a duplicate when BOTH mates match).
param.option: Single dataset (or a list to map per element)
Paired collection (forward/reverse; one run per pair)

param.name: input_file
param.label: Raw read data from your current history

param.name: generate_summary
param.label: Generate summary output of QC test results

param.name: input_pair
param.label: Paired reads
param.help: A paired (forward/reverse) collection analysed as one sample, or a list:paired to analyse each pair independently. SAM/BAM input is not supported in paired mode.

param.label: Per-sample raw data (fastqc_data.txt) to keep
param.help: 'Separate mates' reports forward and reverse separately (two MultiQC samples per pair); 'Combined' pools R1+R2 into a single report (one MultiQC sample per pair); 'Both' keeps all three. The combined HTML report and the paired duplication report are produced either way.

param.label: Assay / library type for pass/warn/fail grading
param.help: FastQC-style grading assumes whole-genome shotgun data and mis-flags expected assay biology (e.g. amplicon duplication, RNA-seq GC bias) as failures. Selecting the assay relaxes ONLY the affected modules; the reported data are unchanged, only the grades and explanatory #Assay comments differ. 'generic' is byte-identical to stock falco. wgbs/emseq/rrbs imply bisulfite handling.

param.label: Incomplete-conversion warning threshold (methylation assays only)
param.help: Residual unmethylated-base fraction above which a possible incomplete-conversion warning is emitted. Only used with assay wgbs/emseq/rrbs; heuristic only, the authoritative check is the post-alignment non-CpG conversion rate.

param.name: contaminants
param.label: Contaminant list
param.help: Tab-delimited file with 2 columns: name and sequence. For example: Illumina Small RNA RT Primer CAAGCAGAAGACGGCATACGA

param.label: Adapter list
param.help: List of adapter sequences which will be explicitly searched against the library. Tab-delimited file with 2 columns: name and sequence.

param.name: limits
param.label: Submodule and limit specifying file
param.help: A file that specifies which submodules are to be executed (default=all) and the thresholds for each submodule's warning parameter.

param.label: Disable grouping of bases for reads >50bp
param.help: Using this option, your plots may end up a ridiculous size. You have been warned!

param.label: Subsampling factor
param.help: Makes the run faster (but possibly less accurate) by only processing reads whose index is a multiple of this value (0-based).

param.label: Bisulfite sequencing
param.help: Reads are from whole genome bisulfite sequencing: the expected increase in Ts and decrease in Cs is accounted for in the base content module. Selecting assay wgbs/emseq/rrbs enables this automatically.

param.name: reverse_complement
param.label: Reverse complement
param.help: The input is reverse-complemented; all modules are tested by swapping A/T and C/G.

tool.help:
**What it does**
falcoAmadeus_ is a performance-focused, sequencing-aware fork of falco (itself a fast C++ reimplementation of FastQC) for quality control of sequencing data. Its default single-end output is byte-identical to falco, and the ``fastqc_data.txt`` raw data output is ingestible by MultiQC as a FastQC report.
On top of the falco/FastQC feature set it adds:
- **Correct paired-end analysis**: forward and reverse mates are analysed together in one run. Besides the usual per-mate reports, a lockstep pass over both mates writes a paired duplication report in which a read pair only counts as a PCR duplicate when *both* mates match, avoiding the systematic overcounting of naive single-end deduplication. A combined HTML report covers forward, reverse and pooled data. - **Assay-aware grading**: FastQC-style pass/warn/fail grading assumes whole-genome shotgun data and mis-flags expected assay biology (amplicon duplication, RNA-seq GC bias, small RNA length distributions, bisulfite base content) as failures. Selecting the assay/library type relaxes only the affected modules; the reported data are unchanged, only the grades plus explanatory ``#Assay`` comments differ. - **Multi-threaded parsing** of plain, gzipped and BAM input, with output byte-identical to a single-threaded run.
**Inputs and outputs**
Single mode accepts FASTQ, FASTQ.gz, SAM or BAM datasets (or a list collection to map over). Paired mode accepts a paired (or list:paired) collection of FASTQ/FASTQ.gz datasets.
The tool produces an HTML report and the FastQC-compatible raw data text file containing Basic Statistics, per-base/per-sequence quality, base and GC content, N content, length distribution, duplication levels, overrepresented sequences and adapter content. In paired mode the paired duplication report and (optionally) per-mate and/or pooled raw data files are produced as well.
Optionally, custom contaminant, adapter and limits files can be supplied, in the same formats FastQC and falco use.
.. _falcoAmadeus: https://github.com/joachimwolff/falcoAmadeus
